name.description: The resource's name. It identifies the resource in request paths and cannot be changed. On create, the name must use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, start with a letter, and end with a letter or digit (`^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$`).

uid.description: A unique identifier the server assigns to the resource when it is created.

resourceVersion.description: The version of the resource's spec. The server increments it each time the spec changes.

createdAt.description: When the resource was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the resource was last changed, in UTC.

deletedAt.description: When the resource's deletion was requested, in UTC. Absent while the resource is not being deleted.

labels.description: Key-value pairs attached to the resource.

annotations.description: Additional information attached to the resource as key-value pairs.

spec.title: AppSpec
spec.description: The desired state of an App.

projectId.description: Server-derived from the request path; the client-supplied value is ignored.

protocol.description: Selects the application-channel protocol the sidecar uses to communicate with the app endpoint: "http" (default) or "grpc".

endpoint.title: AppSpecEndpoint
endpoint.description: The reachable URL of the user's application workload.

token.description: Authenticates calls from the dataplane to the app endpoint. It can only be written; responses never include it (a generated token is returned once as status.appToken).

maxBodySize.description: Overrides the project-level maximum body size for HTTP and gRPC requests handled by this App (e.g. "4Mi", "8Mi", "16Mi").

appChannelTimeoutSeconds.description: The timeout in seconds for the sidecar to connect to the application endpoint. Zero or absent uses the server default.

healthCheck.title: AppSpecHealthCheck
healthCheck.description: Configures how the sidecar checks that the app is healthy.

path.description: The HTTP path probed, for example /healthz. Used with the http protocol only.

probe.title: AppSpecHealthCheckProbe
probe.description: Sets how the sidecar probes the app's health.

intervalInSec.description: The time between probes, in seconds.

timeoutInMs.description: How long a probe may take before it counts as failed, in milliseconds.

failureThreshold.description: The number of failed probes in a row after which the app is reported unhealthy.

appConfig.description: Names the Dapr Configuration this App loads, for example to set tracing, access control or feature flags. Omitting it on an update leaves the current binding in place; an empty string removes it.

workflowArchive.title: AppSpecWorkflowArchive
workflowArchive.description: Selects which terminal workflow states have their history archived on purge and where the archive is written. Archiving is enabled when a destination binding is set.

completed.description: Archives workflows that reach the Completed terminal state.

failed.description: Archives workflows that reach the Failed terminal state.

terminated.description: Archives workflows that reach the Terminated terminal state.

binding.description: The output-binding component name. Empty disables archiving.

workflowNotifications.title: AppSpecWorkflowNotifications
workflowNotifications.description: Selects which workflow outcomes raise an alert. Completed workflows are not selectable: the policy reports outcomes that need someone's attention.

name.description: A regular expression the workflow name must match in full. Empty matches every workflow.

failed.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Failed terminal state.

terminated.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Terminated terminal state.

stalled.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Stalled state.

rootOnly.description: Restricts notifications to workflows with no parent, so one failing parent does not also alert for each of its children.

workflowApi.description: The API this App's workflows use: "dapr" (the default) or "temporal". With "temporal", Temporal SDK clients connect to the project's gRPC endpoint, status.endpoints.grpc, using the App's name as the namespace and its API token as the API key. It needs a region that supports it and a project with a workflow store, and it cannot be changed later.

status.description: The observed state of an App.
The current processing status of the resource.

updatedAt.description: The time of the last status update.

messages.description: Contains any status messages, such as error details.

cluster.description: The name of the cluster that runs this instance in the region. In a public region or a dedicated region it is a cluster Diagrid operates; in a private region it is one of the clusters you joined to the region.

region.description: The region where the instance is located (e.g. "us-east-1").

placementId.description: The project placement this instance belongs to (e.g. "1").

status.description: The current processing status of the resource.

updatedAt.description: The time of the last status update.

messages.description: Contains any status messages, such as error details.

instances.description: Includes the status for each instance of the resource

apiToken.description: Deprecated: read the API token from the embedded backing App ID under status.appIds (request the App with include=appids) instead. appToken.description: Deprecated: read the app token from the embedded backing App ID under status.appIds (request the App with include=appids) instead. Retained for backward compatibility. Omitted when the App has no endpoint, and unless the caller has the appIdCredentials.get permission, or appIdCredentials.list in a list response.

endpointStatus.description: Reports app-endpoint connectivity — "connected", "disconnected" or "unknown". Empty when the App has no endpoint.

items.title: AppStatusAppIdsItem
items.description: An App ID: the identity a workload uses to connect to Catalyst.

apiVersion.description: The API group and version of the resource, for example cra.diagrid.io/v1beta1.

kind.description: The type of the resource, for example AppIdentity.

name.description: The resource's name. It identifies the resource in request paths and cannot be changed.

statusVersion.description: The version of the resource's status. The server increments it each time the status changes.

createdAt.description: When the resource was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the resource was last changed, in UTC.

deletedAt.description: When the resource's deletion was requested, in UTC. Absent while the resource is not being deleted.

finalizers.description: Finalizers name the cleanup steps that must finish before a deleted resource is removed.

annotations.description: Additional information attached to the resource as key-value pairs.

hash.description: A hash of the resource's content, computed by the server.

labels.description: Key-value pairs attached to the resource.

apiTokenRevision.description: The revision of the App ID's API token. Set it to a value higher than the current one to issue a new API token.

appEndpoint.description: The application endpoint configuration of an App ID.

probe.title: AppSpecHealthCheckProbe

failureThreshold.description: The number of failed probes in a row after which the app is reported unhealthy.

protocol.description: The protocol used to call the app endpoint: "http" (the default) or "grpc".

appConfig.description: Names the Dapr Configuration the App ID loads, for example to set tracing, access control or feature flags.

resiliency.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemSpecResiliency

maxBodySize.description: Overrides the project's maximum body size for HTTP and gRPC requests handled by the App ID, for example "4Mi" or "16Mi".

external.description: Marks an App ID whose workload connects to the data plane from outside Catalyst, using status.externalBootstrapConfig. It cannot be changed after creation.

appContainer.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemSpecAppContainer
appContainer.description: The container Catalyst runs next to the App ID's sidecar. It is set by Catalyst for App IDs it manages; a request that sets it is rejected.

port.description: The port the container listens on.

args.description: The arguments passed to the command.

env.description: Environment variables set in the container, by name.

files.description: Files mounted read-only into the container's /app directory, keyed by file name.

completed.description: Archives workflows that reach the Completed terminal state.

failed.description: Archives workflows that reach the Failed terminal state.

terminated.description: Archives workflows that reach the Terminated terminal state.

binding.description: The output-binding component name. Empty disables archiving.

workflowNotifications.title: AppSpecWorkflowNotifications
workflowNotifications.description: Selects which workflow outcomes raise an alert. Completed workflows are not selectable: the policy reports outcomes that need someone's attention.

failed.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Failed terminal state.

terminated.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Terminated terminal state.

stalled.description: Notifies workflows that reach the Stalled state.

resiliencyStatus.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyStatus
resiliencyStatus.description: The resiliency policies applied to the App ID.

resiliency.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliency
resiliency.description: The desired state of a resiliency resource.

projectId.description: The name of the project. Set by the server from the request path.

resiliencySpec.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpec
resiliencySpec.description: The Dapr resiliency specification (policies and targets), based on the upstream Dapr Resiliency API. Fields present upstream but not listed here are not supported in Catalyst.

policies.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecPolicies
policies.description: The named policies that targets refer to.

timeouts.description: Timeout policies: a name mapped to a duration such as 5s.

policy.description: "constant" (a fixed wait between retries) or "exponential" (a wait that grows with each retry).

duration.description: The wait between retries of a constant policy, such as 5s.

maxInterval.description: The longest wait between retries of an exponential policy, such as 60s.

maxRetries.description: The number of retries. -1 retries without limit.

matching.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecPoliciesRetriesMatching
matching.description: Specifies which status codes should trigger a retry. When set, only matching errors are retried; unmatched errors (e.g. 403) fail immediately instead of being retried into a timeout.

httpStatusCodes.description: The HTTP status codes to retry, as a comma-separated list of codes and ranges such as "429,500-504".

gRPCStatusCodes.description: The gRPC status codes to retry, as a comma-separated list of codes and ranges such as "1-4,8-11".

maxRequests.description: The number of requests let through while the circuit is half-open.

interval.description: How often the failure counts are reset while the circuit is closed, such as 60s.

timeout.description: How long the circuit stays open before it becomes half-open, such as 30s.

trip.description: The condition that opens the circuit, for example "consecutiveFailures > 5".

targets.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecTargets
targets.description: Targets apply policies to App IDs and components.

additionalProperties.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecTargetsApps
additionalProperties.description: Holds the names of the policies applied to calls to an App ID.

timeout.description: The name of a timeout policy.

retry.description: The name of a retry policy.

circuitBreaker.description: The name of a circuit breaker policy.

circuitBreakerCacheSize.description: The number of circuit breakers kept for the App ID's instances.

apps.description: Holds the policies applied to calls to an App ID, keyed by App ID name.

additionalProperties.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecTargetsComponents
additionalProperties.description: Holds the names of the policies applied to a component, by direction.

inbound.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecTargetsComponentsInbound
inbound.description: Holds the name of one policy of each kind.

timeout.description: The name of a timeout policy.

retry.description: The name of a retry policy.

circuitBreaker.description: The name of a circuit breaker policy.

outbound.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusResiliencyResiliencySpecTargetsComponentsInbound
outbound.description: Holds the name of one policy of each kind.

timeout.description: The name of a timeout policy.

retry.description: The name of a retry policy.

circuitBreaker.description: The name of a circuit breaker policy.

components.description: Holds the policies applied to a component, keyed by component name.

scopes.description: The App IDs that load the resiliency policies. Empty means every App ID in the project.

spiffeId.description: The single workload identity this App ID is reported under: the identity it is issued in the first of its project's regions by name. It does not move when a region is promoted, and a workload running in any other region of the project presents a different identity. Use regionIdentities to pre-trust the identity of every region instead of following this one.

spiffeIds.description: Every workload identity this App ID is issued, one per region its project is placed in, in the same order as regionIdentities. Deprecated: use regionIdentities instead, which names the region each identity belongs to.

items.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusRegionIdentitiesItem
items.description: An App ID's workload identity in one region.

region.description: The region the identity is issued in. Read that region to get the OIDC issuer verifying JWTs minted for this identity, and the trust anchors verifying its certificates: both are region properties, served on the region's own status.endpoints.

spiffeId.description: The SPIFFE ID workloads of this App ID present in that region.

regionIdentities.description: Lists the workload identity this App ID is issued in every region its project is placed in, one entry per region, ordered by region name. It is spiffeIds with the region each identity belongs to named, so a reader does not have to take it from the trust domain. Pre-trust every entry in an external identity federation: a project spread over a region group runs under a different identity in each of its regions, and which one a workload presents follows the region it runs in. The OIDC issuer that verifies JWTs minted for an identity is the region's, and is read from that region (status.endpoints.oidc).

externalBootstrapConfig.description: The bootstrap YAML configuration for an external App ID. It contains everything an external workload needs to connect to the data plane, including the required endpoints and the join token, so it is omitted unless the caller has the appIdCredentials.get permission, or appIdCredentials.list in a list response.

isActive.description: Indicates if the App ID is active, if the sidecar has performed API operations recently

workflowsConnected.description: Indicates if the App ID has workflow workers currently connected. It is only set when requested with include=workflowStatus, and is absent when that is unknown (no workers-connected metric series for the App ID).

clientType.description: The identity-view classification of this App ID — "app", "agent", or "mcpserver".

appHealthCheckStatus.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusAppHealthCheckStatus
appHealthCheckStatus.description: The result of the latest health check of the App ID's application.

ishealthy.description: Whether the application passed the health check.

reason.description: Explains why the application is not healthy.

events.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusEvents
events.description: Recent events reported by the App ID's sidecar.

items.title: AppStatusAppIdsItemStatusEventsErrorsItem
items.description: One event reported by the App ID's sidecar.

cluster.description: The name of the cluster the event originated from. In a public region or a dedicated region it is a cluster Diagrid operates; in a private region it is one of the clusters you joined to the region.

appIds.description: Embeds the App's backing App ID, including its credentials (status.apiToken and status.appToken). Populated only when a Get request carries include=appids — matching Agent, DurableAgent and MCPServer, and the forward-compatible source for the deprecated inline token fields above.
